topic: Research: Claude Fable 5 Cost Optimization: When to Use vs Opus 4.8 vs Haiku (2026)

key_points: Frames Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 as $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, exactly 2x Opus 4.8 and 10x Haiku 4.5.
Highlights prompt caching at 90% off input and Batch API at 50% off as the main practical levers for reducing effective spend.
Includes a useful pricing table across Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, and Haiku 4.5.
Positions Fable 5 as a premium model for complex coding, scientific, and agentic workflows rather than general chat.
States the API model name is claude-fable-5 and emphasizes the 1,000,000-token context window.
Uses benchmark claims such as SWE-Bench Pro leadership to justify why teams may pay double Opus 4.8 for hard tasks.
Explains input versus output token billing and the $10/$50 per million token pricing in simple buyer terms.
Focuses on subscription access and the original June 22 promotional access cutoff for Claude.ai plans.
Warns readers that API usage has no free tier and that production teams should prefer predictable API billing over uncertain subscription limits.
Makes model routing the central cost optimization tactic: reserve top models for tasks where complexity, risk, or ambiguity justifies the cost.
Positions Haiku as the default for fast, low-risk, high-volume work and Opus as the middle ground for complex but not extreme tasks.
Provides an angle the article should improve on with concrete routing rules, fallback thresholds, and cost formulas.
Compares Fable 5 and Mythos 5 pricing against Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5, emphasizing that Fable 5 output costs can dominate monthly bills.
Treats Fable 5 as a specialist model whose ROI depends on fewer retries, fewer human review cycles, and better first-pass completion.
Useful competitor gap: cost examples should separate input-heavy retrieval workloads from output-heavy agent workflows.

stats.fact: Anthropic lists Claude Fable 5 as currently unavailable as of the June 12, 2026 suspension update, but still publishes pricing of $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

Anthropic says the US government directive required suspending access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for any foreign national, causing Anthropic to disable both models for all customers; other Anthropic models were not affected.

The launch announcement priced Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, and said flagged cybersecurity, biology, or chemistry requests on Fable 5 would be answered by Claude Opus 4.8 instead.
Anthropic's model overview lists Claude Opus 4.8 at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, with a 1M-token context window and 128k max output on the Claude API.
Anthropic's model overview lists Claude Haiku 4.5 at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, with a 200k-token context window and 64k max output.
Claude Fable 5 prompt-cache hits receive the existing 90% input-token discount, making repeated long context workloads materially cheaper when caching applies.
US-only inference for Claude Fable 5 is listed at 1.1x pricing for both input and output tokens.

Claude Haiku 4.5 launched at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens and was described by Anthropic as near-frontier performance with much greater cost efficiency, including 4-5x faster performance than Sonnet 4.5 in one partner quote.

angles: Lead with the June 12 availability caveat: Fable 5 cost optimization is currently a planning and fallback-routing topic until access is restored.

Use a three-tier routing framework: Haiku 4.5 for cheap/high-volume tasks, Opus 4.8 for complex production work, Fable 5 only for long-horizon tasks where better autonomy reduces retries or human hours.
Show effective-cost math, not just list prices: Fable 5 is 2x Opus 4.8 and 10x Haiku 4.5 before caching, but cached repeated context can narrow the input-side gap.
Separate input-heavy and output-heavy workloads because Fable 5 output at $50/MTok is the most dangerous cost driver.
Add a safety/reroute section: flagged Fable 5 domains can fall back to Opus 4.8, which changes both capability and cost expectations.
Recommend instrumentation: log input tokens, output tokens, cache hits, retry rate, escalation rate, and human review time before moving workloads up-model.
Give developers a concrete policy table instead of vague advice: default model, escalation trigger, max budget guardrail, and downgrade path.
